title: Uncertainty and Variability in Shot Peening Process Control Almen Strips, Saturation Curves, Verification and Usable Tolerance
content: Shot peening is controlled through a chain of standards, SAE J442, J443 and J2597, AMS2430 and AMS2432, AMS2431, J444 and J2277, none of which quantifies the uncertainty of its result. This paper sets out an uncertainty model for the chain and a register of reference values with their evidence, built from the J2597 reference data, a replicated experiment of 388 strips, thirty published curves, published process data and simulation. It separates measurement uncertainty from the process variation the strip must detect, and the absolute budget of a set-up from the relative budget of verification. At 0.0126 in A a single reading confirms conformity, with 95% probability under the stated model, only within ±0.0007 in of a ±0.0015 in tolerance, and a verification strip from another lot than its reference only within ±0.0005 in; the usable range closes at high intensity, first on thin and on standard-grade strips. Strip lot and hardness, shot-size latitude, impact angle and machine type are quantified, and changes of flow and stand-off are shown to be misread as changes of intensity by a single strip. Curve equations, Bayesian curve formation, two-exposure verification, transfer between strip types and electronic devices are evaluated, and decision rules, algorithms, recommendations and a strip-measurement programme are proposed.
